questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the key difference between data governance and governance architecture?
options: Governance is the decision about who decides and what the rule is; governance architecture is the system that makes that decision real
Governance only applies to small companies; architecture only applies to large ones
Governance architecture is a job title, not a technical discipline
They are two names for the exact same activity
questions.explain: Governance is the decision (who decides, what the rule is); governance architecture is the system that implements it day to day.

questions.q: Which three layers does this lesson say every governance architecture has to provide?
options: Frontend, backend, and database only
Metadata and catalog, policy and enforcement, and integration
Hiring, training, and performance review
Marketing, sales, and finance
questions.explain: The lesson names three required layers: metadata/catalog, policy/enforcement, and integration.

questions.q: How does the lesson describe governance architecture's relationship to the operating model (Foundations Lessons 10-12)?
options: Architecture replaces the need for an operating model entirely
The operating model is chosen only after all architecture is fully built
Architecture implements the operating model decision; it doesn't replace it
They are unrelated and never interact
questions.explain: Governance architecture builds the systems that make a chosen operating model's decisions real — it doesn't substitute for that decision.

questions.q: What discipline does the lesson compare governance architecture to, as a 'specialized domain inside enterprise architecture'?
options: Sales operations
Graphic design
Security architecture
Payroll administration
questions.explain: The lesson draws the comparison to security architecture — a specialized domain inside enterprise architecture, not a separate bolted-on discipline.

questions.q: According to the lesson, do a centralized and a federated operating model need different layers, or different versions of the same layers?
options: Different versions of the same three layers — metadata, policy, and integration still have to exist either way
Completely unrelated sets of layers with no overlap
Neither model needs a metadata layer
Only the federated model needs any architecture at all
questions.explain: The lesson states both models still need a metadata layer, a policy layer, and an integration layer — just built very differently, which Chapter 2 covers.
